key_insight: Manufacturing-oriented simplification of a generatively designed UAV tail boom reduced mass by 4% and print time by 20%, eliminated supports, and retained load-bearing adequacy under the analyzed quasi-static loads.
engineering_relevance: Adapting organic generative designs to FFF constraints can improve manufacturability without compromising assessed structural adequacy in this case.
method: Compared topology-faithful and simplified variants of the same generative design.
Evaluated both using linear static and buckling FEA under identical loads.
Printed scaled simplified prototypes with two bounding infill configurations and load-tested them.
evidence_signal: Simplification increased peak FEA stress by 31%, but it remained below 2% of the assumed ultimate tensile strength; predicted stress concentrations qualitatively matched observed fracture locations.
watch_item: Results are case-specific: scaled prototype tests and quasi-static analyses do not establish full-scale performance under fatigue, dynamic loading, or FFF material variability.
paper_title: Post-processing strategies for generative design outcomes in a UAV tail boom
